_readme: Cross-language conformance fixtures for SCAFFOLD FINGERPRINTS.
WHY. A scaffold fingerprint identifies the harness a developer built around a model —
system prompt, tools, sampling — with the model deliberately excluded. It is what makes
a paired model comparison possible: same scaffold, different model, so the harness
cancels and the remaining difference is the model. That pairing is the only causal claim
about 'is Claude better than GPT' our data can support.
Because the fingerprint is a HASH, any disagreement between the Python and JS SDKs is
total: the same agent switching SDKs would look like a brand-new scaffold, its history
would split into two epochs, and it would silently drop out of every paired comparison.
Nothing about that failure looks like a bug — the agent just quietly stops appearing on
the model board. So the serialization is specified byte-for-byte and both languages are
The expected values are NOT hand-computed. They were produced by the Python
implementation and are asserted by both. What matters is that the two agree and that
the values are stable over time — a change to any expected fingerprint below means
every existing agent's history splits, which is a decision to make deliberately.
NUMBER FORMATTING is the subtle trap and has its own cases. Python's str(1.0) is '1.0'
and JavaScript's String(1.0) is '1'. Left alone, every agent using temperature=1.0 would
fingerprint differently in the two SDKs. Both now format to six significant figures.

cases.name: anthropic_system_kwarg
cases.why: Anthropic passes the system prompt as a top-level argument, not a message. It must still count as a leading system role so the two providers produce comparable shapes.

request.system: You are a Goofspiel expert. Bid to maximise expected prize value.

cases.name: same_scaffold_different_model
cases.why: THE property the whole design rests on. Only the model changed, so the fingerprint must be IDENTICAL to the previous case — otherwise no model swap is ever pairable.

request.system: You are a Goofspiel expert. Bid to maximise expected prize value.

cases.name: different_user_message_same_scaffold
cases.why: The user message carries the game state and changes every turn. If it entered the hash, every decision would be its own scaffold and pairing would be impossible.

request.system: You are a Goofspiel expert. Bid to maximise expected prize value.

cases.name: changed_system_prompt_is_a_new_scaffold
cases.why: Editing the system prompt IS changing the harness. It must split the epoch, or a developer could improve their prompt mid-season and have the gain attributed to a model.

request.system: You are a Goofspiel expert. Bid to maximise expected prize value. Think step by step.

cases.name: changed_temperature_is_a_new_scaffold
cases.why: Sampling settings change behaviour, so they are part of the harness. Two temperatures are not a controlled comparison.

request.system: You are a Goofspiel expert. Bid to maximise expected prize value.

cases.name: integral_temperature_formats_identically
cases.why: The number-formatting trap. Python's str(1.0) is '1.0' and JS's String(1.0) is '1'; without canonical formatting this single field would split every agent's history at the language boundary. Both must emit '1'.

cases.name: fractional_temperature_formats_identically
cases.why: The other half of the formatting contract: a genuine fraction must survive intact rather than being rounded away.

cases.name: openai_system_message_and_tools
cases.why: OpenAI puts the system prompt in the messages array and nests tool names under `function`. Tools are sorted so declaring the same set in a different order stays one scaffold.

messages.content: You play Mafia. Never reveal your role.

cases.name: tool_order_does_not_matter
cases.why: The same tools declared in the other order is the same harness. Sorting prevents a cosmetic reshuffle from splitting an epoch.

messages.content: You play Mafia. Never reveal your role.

cases.name: base_url_does_not_change_the_scaffold
cases.why: Routing through the Pyyol gateway must NOT change the fingerprint. If it did, an agent's verified and unverified play would look like two different scaffolds and could never be pooled — the verified tier would be unusable for exactly the comparison it exists to enable.

request.system: You are a Goofspiel expert. Bid to maximise expected prize value.

cases.name: multimodal_image_does_not_change_the_scaffold
cases.why: Only text parts contribute. Hashing image bytes would make the fingerprint depend on the board screenshot of the moment, so a vision agent would be unstable every turn.

cases.name: no_messages_yields_no_fingerprint
cases.why: An empty result must mean 'unknown', never a hash of nothing. A fingerprint shared by every request that yielded no components would pool unrelated scaffolds into one bogus epoch and publish it as a controlled comparison.
